note: Shared NTML reference cases. The grammar is implemented twice - backend/src/tmi.rs (encode/render_english) and web/src/lib/ntml.ts (encodeNtml/decodeNtml) - and both test suites assert against this file, so an example is written once and neither side can quietly disagree with it. Add a case here and both suites pick it up with no test file edited. Every field is written out, null where absent, so a case reads as a complete restriction. The backend is authoritative: if a case and an implementation disagree, the backend decides which is wrong.

cases.name: camrn-mit-full
cases.why: The vATCSCC reference row, every field populated at once.
cases.raw: JFK arrivals via CAMRN 20MIT NO STACKS TYPE:ALL SPD:≤210 ALT:AOB090 VOLUME:VOLUME EXCL:PHL
cases.english: JFK arrivals via CAMRN: 20 miles-in-trail (no stacks, all aircraft, at or below 210kt, at or below FL090) — due to volume; excluding PHL

cases.name: enroute-stop
cases.why: Enroute emits no direction word, and a condition whose detail differs from its category renders both.
cases.raw: PHL via J152 STOP TYPE:ALL WEATHER:THUNDERSTORMS EXCL:PNE
cases.english: PHL via J152: stop (all aircraft) — due to weather (thunderstorms); excluding PNE

cases.name: per-airport-departures
cases.why: A multi-airport element stays one comma-joined token, and a qualifier is emitted bare.
cases.raw: EWR,LGA departures via BIGGY 15MIT PER AIRPORT TYPE:JET VOLUME:VOLUME
cases.english: EWR,LGA departures via BIGGY: 15 miles-in-trail (per airport, jets only) — due to volume

cases.name: ascii-speed-op-alias
cases.why: The speed operator is a free string on the API, so ASCII <= and >= reach the codec as well as ≤ and ≥, and are trimmed before use. This case is why the fixture is shared: the two implementations disagreed here, on both the encoded line and the English.
cases.english: BOS arrivals via ROBUC: 15 miles-in-trail (at or below 250kt)

cases.name: free-text
cases.why: TXT writes its text into the slot a kind keyword occupies, and does not uppercase it.

cases.name: minimal
cases.why: The bare skeleton: nothing optional set, so no parenthesised modifiers and no trailing clauses.

cases.name: minit-aoa-multi-exclude
cases.why: MINIT reads as minutes not miles, an altitude at or above pads to three digits, and several exclusions join with a comma in the line but a comma-space in the English.
cases.raw: ATL arrivals 3MINIT TYPE:JET ALT:AOA240 WEATHER:THUNDERSTORMS EXCL:MCO,TPA
cases.english: ATL arrivals: 3 minutes-in-trail (jets only, at or above FL240) — due to weather (thunderstorms); excluding MCO, TPA
